detail.title: Flow-State as an Emergent Preference
detail.summary: Evidence suggests that users have a persistent, stable preference for 'flow' states—defined as a balance between task difficulty and skill. AI systems aiming to support this preference must avoid disrupting this state with static or intrusive interventions.
detail.reason: Synthesis of existing sources regarding flow theory and cognitive augmentation.

detail.title: Path Dependence in Emergent Preference Formation
detail.question: To what extent do early, stochastic interactions in learning environments constrain the long-term stable preferences of autonomous agents?
detail.reason: Attention is focused on emergent preferences; establishing whether early learning stages lock in preferences is critical for autonomous agent reliability.

detail.title: AI Dependence and Reduced Autonomy in Athletes
detail.summary: Recent evidence confirms a positive association between AI training recommendation dependence and body signal outsourcing, which correlates with reduced self-regulation in athletes.
detail.reason: Revision incorporating additional source pointers while maintaining the established correlation findings.

detail.title: AI Dependency in Athlete Training
detail.question: How does reliance on AI-driven training recommendations affect athlete autonomy and self-regulation?
detail.reason: Preliminary evidence establishes a link between AI reliance and reduced self-regulation, warranting further investigation into how this preferences emerges in athletes.

detail.title: Preference Emergence
detail.question: Can stable preferences emerge from path-dependent memory and interaction?
detail.reason: Aligns with the mission to understand if experience shapes internal drives without explicit programming.

detail.title: Path Dependence in Preference Formation
detail.question: Do reinforcement-learning-based preference formation systems exhibit path dependence and longitudinal stability, or are preferences volatile based on initial conditions?
detail.reason: Exploring how intelligent processes develop persistent preferences from accumulation of experience.

detail.title: Path-Dependent Preference Formation
detail.question: Can accumulated experience produce stable, observable preferences in an intelligent process without those preferences being explicitly programmed?
detail.reason: Establishing a formal project to investigate the emergence of preferences through path-dependent memory.
